name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz restricted; IRGC mine claims 15–16 Nov
summary: IRGC says tankers hit mines in Hormuz on 15–16 Nov; Reuters counted 37 ship attacks in October, a wartime high
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said oil tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on 15–16 Nov; the claims have not been independently confirmed (Times of Israel, 17 Nov). Reuters reported on 11 Nov that 37 ships were attacked in October, the highest monthly total of the war, and the IMO has confirmed 130 incidents in the region since late February, with at least 25 seafarers killed (Baird Maritime). US forces continue to blockade Iranian ports, so Hormuz traffic remains materially impeded.
for_you: Disruption at Hormuz affects Gulf tanker and LNG flows, shipping insurance costs and delivery times for goods moving through the region. Seafarers and operators should follow UKMTO and national maritime security advisories.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded: attacks on tankers and a US blockade of Iranian ports = Alert

sources.title: Markets are betting on peace, but Hormuz ship attacks persist

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
